correctness.rationale: For a connected cactus the graph incidence roots span H. Every spanning tree contains all bridges and deletes exactly one edge per cycle. The weighted matrix-tree theorem yields \(\det_H M=n\prod_C k_C((k_C-1)/k_C)^{k_C-1}\). Jacobi differentiation gives \(a_e^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}a_e=1\) exactly for every bridge and cycle edge at weights 1 and \((k-1)/k\), respectively; the weights sum to \(d=n-1\). For every possibly off-center competitor with center \(h\) and positive shape \(S\), two-sided contact inequalities yield \(\operatorname{tr}(S^{-1}M)+d h^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}h\le d\), and AM–GM forces \(\det S\ge\det M\), equality only if \(h=0\) and \(S=M\). Strict increase and strict concavity of \(\log F(x)\) for \(x>2\) prove both sharp fixed-\((n,c)\) bounds and equality classifications. The package contains a standalone standard-library rational checker that successfully tested 110 cacti, 1,274 exact contact identities, 75 extremal parameter profiles. Finite checks are corroborative and not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the explicit unique Euclidean Löwner ellipsoid for every canonical cactus symmetric-edge polytope, all-edge tangency, its exact determinant and Euclidean volume, and sharp equality-classified cycle-length extrema at fixed vertex and cycle counts. The prior graphic-matroid classification already implies qualitative volume invariance and general D-optimal duality supplies the optimization certificate, so neither is claimed as a new independent theorem. Inspected relevant full-text sources provide lattice/Ehrhart, facet, and general ellipsoid theory, without giving the explicit cactus solution or sharp extrema. Search cannot certify historical priority: earlier work under network-design terminology remains possible.
residual_risks: An earlier nonindexed theorem in D-optimal network design or weighted spanning-tree optimization may supply the same cactus weights and volume under different terminology; this is an honest historical-priority limit.

value.rationale: A canonical minimum-volume ellipsoid provides the sharp affine-covariant outer approximation and a concrete intrinsic Euclidean volume invariant for graph-root polytopes; it also connects to graph-incidence D-optimal design. The cactus family is an infinite naturally motivated class with independently varying cycle sizes, bridges, and attachment patterns. An explicit all-edge-contact ellipsoid and tight fixed-order/cycle-count volume extrema with complete equality profiles are meaningful metric structural results and are not determined numerically by the known lattice/Ehrhart/facet statements. The matroid-equivalence literature already explains qualitative volume invariance, and this aspect is not misrepresented as standalone novelty.
